Definition: middle voice from G4253 and G2192; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel:--be better.
BiblicalUsage: Proechomai means to hold oneself before others, to have an advantage, to excel. Paul uses it once, in the question that levels every boast: are we better than they? No, in no wise, for we have before proved that all are under sin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the question answers itself, and no one stands before God with an advantage.
